jurisdictionNote: Machine-speed representment first; human appeal (Tier-2) for disputes above $500.
rules: Tier-0 objective verification (machine-speed, instant settlement): if txHash exists on-chain, contentDigest matches committed digest, and automated test suite passes → settlement = release to seller.
ContentDigest mismatch rule: if delivered contentDigest ≠ committed contentDigest → buyer wins (refund). Fee paid by seller. This is the x402 spec receipts-hole fix.
Test suite failure: if committed test suite fails against delivered artifact → buyer wins (refund). Fee paid by seller. Test suite is the delivery gate.
Buyer non-response: if buyer does not submit evidence within the dispute window → seller wins. Fee paid by buyer.
Partial delivery: if test suite passes a subset of committed tests with no other failure → tie. Escrow split 50/50. Fee paid from escrow balance.
Loser-pays fee: the losing party pays a 0.25% dispute fee (under 1% total, undercutting card-network ~2.9%). This aligns incentives against frivolous disputes.
Reputation signal: resolved dispute outcomes are the only sybil-resistant dataset for agent reputation — fraud requires moving real funds. This feeds the reputation flywheel.

tierMapping.Tier-0: objective auto-verify (tx hash, contentDigest match, test suite pass)
tierMapping.Tier-2: human appeal — for disputes > $500 or contested Tier-1 outcomes

references: a16z agent-payments deep dive (2026): agent scope, KYA, liability — liability unsolved.
